clue.text: Overwrought father cut short tomfoolery

parts.note: FR is the standard abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

indicators.note: cut short means the word loses its final letter, here the plural ending

parts.note: antics are silly, clownish capers

explanation.surface: A dad, worn out, puts a stop to the children's silly games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' trims ANTICS to ANTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone overwrought is in a wild, distraught state, which is what frantic describes.

clue.text: Salts perhaps in need of leader after sailor Jack gives up

indicators.note: after places the trimmed word behind the sailor and the jack

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword sailor
J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards

indicators.note: lacking a leader means the word's first letter is missing

parts.note: salting is one way of curing meat, so salts are an example of cures

explanation.surface: Old sailors, short of a captain, hear that a seaman named Jack is quitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in need of leader' takes C from CURES, leaving URES. 'Salts' looks like sailors, but it is a verb-turned-noun for preserving.
explanation.definitionFit: To abjure is to renounce or formally give up a belief or claim.

clue.text: Conversation's sure to founder — dance takes precedence

indicators.note: taking precedence means going first, so the dance comes before the rest

parts.note: a disco is a dance or dance party

indicators.note: to founder is to collapse or go to wreck, so the letters break up and re-form

explanation.surface: Someone's chat is certain to fail, because the dancing matters more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to founder' rearranges the four letters to URSE; 'Conversation's' is the definition with a link 's, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Discourse is formal talk or exchange of ideas, a synonym for conversation.

clue.text: Records unknown label primarily seen on foreign wine

parts.note: vin is French for wine
Y is an algebraic unknown, like X and Z

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the word label counts

explanation.surface: A mystery label is seen mostly on bottles of imported wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinyl is the material of gramophone discs, and collectively it means records.

clue.text: Start missing answer? They say you always pay for it

definitions.text: They say you always pay for it

indicators.note: missing means the abbreviation is taken out of the word for start

parts.note: to launch something is to start it

explanation.surface: A quiz question opens without an answer, and the chuckle says you will pay for it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to the saying 'there's no such thing as a free lunch'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb holds that no midday meal is ever truly free, so this meal is what you always pay for.

clue.text: Shoot sergeant major visiting eastern state commissioner

indicators.note: visiting means going into, so these pieces sit inside the country

parts.note: Oman is a state in the Middle East
a bud is a new shoot on a plant
SM is the military abbreviation for sergeant major

explanation.surface: A young recruit and his sergeant major go on a tour of a Gulf state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'visiting' signals a container; 'eastern state' is one phrase for the Gulf country, not E plus a state.
explanation.definitionFit: An ombudsman is an official commissioner appointed to investigate public complaints.

clue.text: Means to bring up two aspects of contact sport?

definitions.meaning: a pulley system with rope, used to hoist heavy loads
in rugby or American football, blocking and tackling are two physical moves

explanation.definitionFit: A pulley-and-rope hoisting rig is named for its block and its tackle, also two moves in football.

clue.text: What could produce a cheer when lit close to bonfire?

definitions.text: What could produce a cheer when lit close to bonfire?

indicators.note: could produce means these letters can be worked into something new

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A firework at a bonfire party makes the crowd cheer once it is lit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could produce' rearranges ACHEERWHENLIT plus E, the last letter of bonfire from 'close to'. The whole clue also describes the firework.
explanation.definitionFit: A Catherine wheel is a spinning firework, set off on Bonfire Night to cheers.

clue.text: Last couple of men within start smoking to relax

indicators.note: within means those letters go inside the phrase for smoking

parts.note: to light up is to start a cigarette

indicators.note: the last couple means the final two letters of the word men

explanation.surface: The last two men inside light a cigarette to unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within' signals a container; 'start smoking' as a phrase means to light a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: To lighten up is an idiom for to relax and stop being so serious.

clue.text: Nameless, titled person returns, individual wanting contacts?

indicators.note: returns means the remaining letters are read backwards
nameless means N, the abbreviation for name, is removed

parts.note: an eponym is a person whose name gives a title to something

explanation.surface: An anonymous aristocrat comes back, a loner looking for connections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nameless' strips N from EPONYM to leave EPOYM, and 'returns' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-sighted person needs contact lenses, so is wanting contacts in a playful sense.

clue.text: Moving into second place, backmarker in river race

indicators.note: moving into second place means a letter is shifted to position two
the backmarker is the one at the rear, here the final letter of the river

parts.note: the Tiber is the river of Rome

explanation.surface: In a river race, the backmarker moves up into second place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backmarker' names the last letter R of TIBER, which 'Moving into second place' shifts to become TRIBE. The racing picture is misdirection: race means a people.
explanation.definitionFit: A race in the sense of a people or ethnic group is a tribe.

clue.text: Taking off retro work with artist in final?

indicators.note: retro means going backwards, so the combination is reversed
in puts the artist inside the work

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a musical work
RA is a Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist
dying, as in dying moments, means final

explanation.surface: Someone mocks an old-fashioned piece by an artist who reached the final.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retro' turns the work-with-artist combination round to PARO. 'Taking off' means mimicking, not departing.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking someone off means mimicking them, which is parodying.

clue.text: City doctor needs mobile

indicators.note: mobile means able to move about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A city doctor needs a mobile phone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mobile' rearranges NEEDS to ESDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Dresden is a city in eastern Germany, the capital of Saxony.

clue.text: She's admired by juniors longing to break through

indicators.note: to break through means to burst into, so the longing sits inside

parts.note: through means finished, done
a yen is a longing or yearning

explanation.surface: Young admirers long to break through to a respected woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to break' signals a container; 'through' here means finished, not passing across.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyenne is the most senior and respected woman in a field, looked up to by younger members.

clue.text: Cook's dossier gone into by theologian

indicators.note: gone into by means the theologian goes inside the file

parts.note: a dossier is a file of documents
DD, Doctor of Divinity, is the crossword theologian

explanation.surface: A cook's records are investigated by a churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' is a verb here, as in cooking the books, and 'gone into by' signals a container.
explanation.definitionFit: To cook accounts is to falsify them, which is to fiddle them.

clue.text: Regularly read over elevated passages in magazine

indicators.note: over means turned over, read backwards
regularly means taking alternate letters of the word read
elevated means raised, so in this down clue the word reads upwards

parts.note: lanes are narrow passages

explanation.surface: Every so often someone reads over raised passages in a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes RA from read and 'over' turns it to AR; 'elevated' reverses LANES to SENAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A magazine is a store for weapons and ammunition, just like an arsenal.

clue.text: Warning sign that canine ought to be stopped?

definitions.text: Warning sign that canine ought to be stopped?

parts.words: Warning sign that canine ought to be stopped?
parts.note: the canine is a pointed tooth, not a dog, and stopping it means filling a cavity; the pain is the warning

explanation.definitionFit: An aching canine tooth signals a cavity that a dentist ought to fill, or stop.

clue.text: Area in my allotment causing concern

parts.note: cor is an exclamation of surprise, like my!

indicators.note: in places the area letter inside the allotment

parts.note: an allotment is a portion or share

explanation.surface: Something in a gardener's plot is giving cause for worry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts A inside PORTION to make PORATION. 'Allotment' suggests a garden plot, but it is a share.
explanation.definitionFit: A concern in the business sense is a company, which a corporation is.

clue.text: Large shed by shaft fell

indicators.note: shed means cast off, so the letter for large is removed

parts.note: an axle is the shaft a wheel turns on

explanation.surface: A big shed beside a mineshaft fell down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' takes L out of AXLE. 'fell' looks like a verb, but it is the noun or verb sense of cutting down.
explanation.definitionFit: To fell a tree you use an axe, and to axe something is to cut it down.

clue.text: Event's top three couples in formal attire got up and danced

indicators.note: got up means rising, so in this down clue it reads upwards
in puts the letters inside the jacket

parts.note: DJ, dinner jacket, is formal evening wear

indicators.note: top means the opening letter of the word event

parts.note: three pairs make six, VI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: The leading three pairs at a ball, in black tie, got to their feet and danced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got up' turns the whole container, DEVIJ, upwards in this down clue. 'Event's top' is the first letter of event.
explanation.definitionFit: To jive is to perform a lively swing dance, so jived means danced.

clue.text: A way of working in class got out of control

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the class

parts.note: a rank is a class or grade
MO, modus operandi, is a way of working

explanation.surface: A method used in a classroom spun out of control.
explanation.definitionFit: To run amok is an idiom for going wild and losing control.

clue.text: Breakaway runner changes sides

indicators.note: R and L stand for right and left, so swapping one for the other changes sides

parts.note: a sprinter is a runner

explanation.surface: A breakaway runner moves from one side of the track to the other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes sides' swaps an R (right) for an L (left) in SPRINTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A splinter group is a breakaway faction from a larger body.

clue.text: Peppery fish served up, tougher after heating?

indicators.note: served up means presented upwards, so in this down clue the fish reads backwards

parts.note: a dab is a small flatfish
steel is tempered by heating to make it tougher

explanation.surface: A spicy fish dish is brought to the table, made tougher by cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' reverses DAB to BAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Peppery describes a hot-tempered, irritable person, which is bad-tempered.

clue.text: No pukka journalist on case of lady with red face?

parts.note: something not pukka, not genuine, is a sham
ED, editor, is the crossword journalist

indicators.note: case of means the outside letters of the word lady

explanation.surface: A phoney reporter is embarrassed about the matter of a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' gives LY from lady. Pukka is British slang for genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with a red face means acting in embarrassment, which is acting ashamedly.

clue.text: Brief row leads to program's top exec defending what Moore did

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to scull is to row a boat

indicators.note: leads means the first letters of the following four words

explanation.surface: A short argument leads to a software firm's boss justifying what a man did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' trims SCULL to SCUL and 'leads to' takes PTED from program's top exec defending. Henry Moore was a famous English sculptor.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Moore, the English artist, carved and modelled works in stone and bronze.

clue.text: Singular exits from comic stealing end of joke

indicators.note: comic means funny or absurd, so the remaining letters are jumbled
exits from means the letter leaves the word that follows

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A lone performer quits a comedian who has been pinching punchlines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exits from' removes S from STEALING, and 'comic' rearranges TEALING.
explanation.definitionFit: A tagline is the punchline that closes a joke.

clue.text: Men involved in racket reversing long-term damage

indicators.note: reversing means the combination is read backwards
involved in means put inside the noise

parts.note: a racket is a din, noise
OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Soldiers caught up in a scam are undoing lasting harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' turns the whole container, NOISORE, round.
explanation.definitionFit: Erosion is gradual wearing away over a long period, a slow form of damage.

clue.text: Spare home agreements largely unused

indicators.note: largely unused means most of the letters are thrown away, leaving a run inside these words

explanation.surface: Spare household agreements mostly go unused.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare in the sense of lean or scanty means meagre.

clue.text: Walk, or drift, horse having bolted

indicators.note: having bolted means the horse has run off, so its letter is removed

parts.note: the thread of an argument is its drift
H is slang for heroin, itself called horse

explanation.surface: A stroll or just wandering after a horse runs off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having bolted' removes H from THREAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A tread is a step or the act of walking.

clue.text: Begin removing old bird cage

indicators.note: removing means the old letter is taken away

parts.note: to open is to begin

explanation.surface: Begin by taking the old bird out of its cage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing' takes O from OPEN. 'bird' is a second definition: a pen is a female swan.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen is an enclosure for animals, a kind of cage.
